paper_title: MathOdyssey Benchmarking Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills in Large   Language Models Using Odyssey Math Data
caption: There are three answer-types: True-False questions, Multiple-Choice questions and Open-Answer questions.
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of three answer types—True-False, Multiple-Choice, and Open-Answer—within the MathOdyssey benchmark dataset, which is used to evaluate mathematical problem-solving skills in large language models. The chart is divided into three colored segments: the largest, in green, represents Open-Answer questions (244 items, 63.0% of the total); the orange segment corresponds to Multiple-Choice questions (127 items, 32.8%); and the smallest, in blue, indicates True-False questions (16 items, 4.1%). Each slice is labeled with both the category name and its count, and percentage values are displayed inside the respective segments. To the right of the chart, examples of each question type are provided, including an Open-Answer problem involving prime numbers, a Multi-Choice algebraic equation, and a True-False hypothesis testing question, reinforcing the diversity of mathematical reasoning assessed in the benchmark.
